Hi Sarah / team,

Thanks again for the deep dive last week. Attached are three short scenarios (tabbed in the workbook) that try to balance: (1) getting you predictable year-over-year economics, (2) smoothing the end-of-year credit cliffs you called out, and (3) giving you headroom to add capacity in Q1 without heavy overage risk.

High-level options in the workbook (attached):
- Smoothing + Co-term: Aligns to a Jan 1 cycle, small upfront credit to cover Q1 start, 24-month term with gradual ramp buckets.
- Upsize with Phased Billing: 36-month commitment, lower unit price, but staged unlocks tied to quarterly usage thresholds.
- Burst-friendly Annual: 12-month term, credit buffer for seasonal bursts, optional prepay for Q1.

Key asks from our side to pick the right path:
1) Which date do you prefer as the contract effective date (Jan 1 vs Feb 1)?
2) Do you want a 2- or 3-year structure for predictable unit pricing?
3) Any internal procurement constraints around auto-renew windows (we can exclude auto-renew if required).

I've also included a simple MOU-style CSV that shows billing start vs capacity unlocks for the phased option. If you prefer, we can convert the chosen scenario into an amendment and a mutual action plan for signatures.

Attachments: Acme_Renewal_Scenario_Options.xlsx (3 tabs) — MOU-Acme-Q1-burst.csv 

Next step proposal: pick one scenario this week, we’ll produce an amendment + redline-friendly term sheet by next Wed (23 Nov).

Sarah — quick answers inline and a recommended path from our side: 

1) Credit mechanics for Jan 1 co-term: the credit in the workbook is modeled as an upfront dollar credit applied to the invoice covering Jan–Mar. We can alternatively apply it as a per-token discount until the credit is exhausted; let us know which you prefer for accounting.

2) 36-month phased pricing: yes, we can fix the unit price for years 2 & 3 in the amendment. We typically include an annual CPI floor/cap (e.g., +/− 3%) — if you want zero variance we can do that as an exception and include it as a contract clause.

Recommended path (our POV): Go with the 24-month co-term with a Q1 buffer credit + a Q1 burst prepay option. Rationale: keeps you on a predictable Jan 1 cadence, gives finance a simpler two-year model, and gives you upsize flexibility via a prepay or a short-notice top-up SKU.

I’ve started a short mutual action plan and an amendment skeleton (will drop to DocuSign once we have a chosen scenario). Link to the MOP: https://app.redwood.com/deals/ACME-2027-RNWL-92
